SUBJECT: ARMS CONTROL CONSULTATIONS WITH ALLIES
TAGS: PARM, MARR, NATO, US

1. (S) Secretary Rogers met with NATO Secretary General Luns on December 28
to review status of mutual and balanced force reductions (MBFR) talks. Allied
position remains coordinated; no major shifts in posture expected before
the January round in Vienna.

2. (S) On strategic arms, Soviet posture appears more flexible following
the November Brezhnev-Nixon summit. Recommend continued close consultation
with Bonn and London on next steps.

SUBJECT: EVACUATION PLANNING UPDATE
TAGS: AEMR, VS, MARR

1. (C) Embassy Saigon reports continued deterioration of military situation
north and west of capital. Ambassador Martin has authorized initial movement
of non-essential personnel and dependents to Manila and Bangkok.

2. (C) Helicopter evacuation contingency (Operation FREQUENT WIND) remains
on standby. Defense attache office reports DAO compound and Tan Son Nhut
remain primary LZs.

SUBJECT: GENERAL ASSEMBLY 40TH SESSION OPENING REMARKS
TAGS: PREL, UNGA, US

1. The 40th regular session of the UN General Assembly opened September 17
under presidency of Spain's Jaime de Pinies. President Reagan addressed
the body September 24 emphasizing US commitment to multilateral diplomacy
on terrorism, narcotics, and human rights.

2. Soviet representative Gromyko's address focused on disarmament and
regional conflict resolution. No surprises in either presentation.

SUBJECT: WMD INSPECTION ACCESS UPDATE
TAGS: PARM, IZ, UNSC

1. (S) UNMOVIC chief Blix reports continued Iraqi cooperation on access to
declared sites but ongoing concerns about completeness of December 7
declaration. Mobile biological labs remain unaccounted for.

2. (S) Embassy assessment: regime is calibrating cooperation level to delay
Security Council consensus on follow-on resolution. Recommend continued
pressure for unrestricted scientist interviews outside Iraq.

SUBJECT: PRIME MINISTER GILANI ON COUNTER-TERROR COOPERATION
TAGS: PREL, PTER, PK, AF, IN

1. (C) Ambassador Patterson met PM Gilani November 6. Gilani reaffirmed
commitment to South Waziristan operation but expressed concern over US
drone strike tempo affecting civilian casualty narrative.

2. (C) On India, Gilani stated Pakistan would not move troops from eastern
border absent reciprocal Indian gesture. Mumbai-related trials proceeding
slowly through Anti-Terrorism Court.
